title: Suriya's ₹304 Crore Blockbuster Karuppu Hits Amazon Prime Thursday. The Wait Is Over.
excerpt: The highest-grossing Tamil film of 2026 — a mythology-meets-courtroom fantasy about a guardian deity who becomes a lawyer — streams in five languages starting June 12. Here's everything the diaspora needs to know.
body:
If you've been hearing about this film for weeks and wondering when you'd actually get to watch it — Thursday is your day. **Karuppu**, **Suriya**'s mythology-drenched courtroom fantasy that obliterated every box office record in sight, premieres on **Amazon Prime Video on June 12**. Globally. In five languages. The diaspora viewing party starts now.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=JpVl_-1YgIo</youtube>

Here's what the fuss is about: Karuppu earned **₹304 crore worldwide** against a ₹130-140 crore budget. It overtook **Singam 2**'s lifetime collection in *four days*. It blew past **Mersal**, **Petta**, and **Thunivu** to become the **highest-grossing Tamil film of 2026** and the highest-grossing film of Suriya's entire career. When the early 28-day streaming window was announced, even trade insiders raised eyebrows — a film this hot doesn't usually leave theatres this fast.

But Amazon Prime wanted it, and they got it. Smart move.

## A God Walks Into a Courtroom

Directed by **RJ Balaji** — who also co-stars and co-wrote the screenplay — *Karuppu* tells the story of **Vettai Karuppu**, a guardian deity from Tamil folklore who disguises himself as a lawyer named Saravanan to fight corruption in a rigged court system. The trigger? A father and daughter from Kerala travel to Chennai for a liver transplant, carrying 60 sovereigns of gold. The gold gets stolen, the police are useless, a corrupt lawyer named **Baby Kannan** (played by Balaji himself, in a performance that's been the talk of Tamil Nadu) exploits the family until they lose everything — and the little girl dies before her surgery.

That's when the deity descends.

What follows is a blazing mix of courtroom drama, mythology, mass action set pieces, and divine justice that feels like Tamil cinema's answer to a Marvel origin story — except rooted in actual folk tradition. The scenes set within Karuppu's divine portal have been compared to a homegrown Dark Dimension. When Suriya switches to his deity avatar, the screen practically vibrates.

## Suriya Has Never Been This Commanding

There's a reason this film became the biggest hit of his 30-year career. **Suriya** at 51 looks like he was carved out of granite specifically for this role — part lawyer, part god, entirely magnetic. The dual performance — measured legal strategist in the courtroom, unstoppable divine force outside it — showcases a range that even his fans didn't know he had.

**Trisha Krishnan** returns as Advocate Preethi in their fourth collaboration, following *Mounam Pesiyadhe* (2002), *Aayutha Ezhuthu* (2004), and *Aaru* (2005). The chemistry remains effortless. She brings warmth and intelligence to a role that could have been a sidekick but instead becomes the film's moral compass.

The supporting cast is loaded: **Indrans** as the heartbroken father, **Natty Subramaniam** as a compromised judge, **Swasika** and **Sshivada** in key roles. And there's a climax cameo that had Tamil audiences screaming — Suriya as **DSP Durai Singam**, reprising his iconic role from the *Singam* series. Fan service? Absolutely. But earned.

## Where to Watch — The Diaspora Guide

**Amazon Prime Video, June 12, 2026.** Launching simultaneously in **240 countries**, which means NRIs in the US, UK, Canada, Australia, and the Middle East can watch on release day.

Available languages:
- **Tamil** (original)
- **Telugu** (titled *Veerabhadrudu*)
- **Malayalam**
- **Kannada**
- **Hindi**

https://www.instagram.com/p/DZUFFW3gDoN/


The music, composed by **Sai Abhyankkar** (who stepped in after **AR Rahman** opted out for undisclosed reasons), has already produced earworms — "God Mode" dropped during Diwali and hasn't left playlists since. The full album landed May 25 and has been streaming steadily.

## The Verdict

Critics gave it mixed-to-positive reviews. The honest take: when Suriya is in deity mode, the film soars — the staging, the visual effects, the sheer mass appeal is undeniable. When it downshifts to the procedural courtroom stretches, it occasionally loses breath. The Cinema Express review captured it best: "Whenever Suriya takes on the Karuppu avatar, the film turns into a veneration of the deity. When the focus isn't on the omnipresent, the film labours to the next mass moment."

But here's the thing: audiences didn't care about the critics. ₹304 crore says everything that needs saying.

For the diaspora, this is the kind of film you watch with family, the kind that makes your parents sit up straighter, the kind where the mythology feels personal. Vettai Karuppu isn't a random superhero. He's a deity your grandmother prayed to. And on Thursday, he's on your living room screen.
